market_holds: Spot $2.06 (Yahoo close 2026-11-24; baseline seal $2.075). No usable option chain (ATM legs not two-sided, baseline), so no implied move. Usual move from my own read of Yahoo daily bars around the last four prints: about -8% (Q3'25, 2025-11-26), about -9% (Q4'25, 2026-03-05), about -10% (Q1'26, 2026-06-02), +5% (Q2'26, 2026-08-27). That is down on 3 of 4 even though revenue beat the top of guidance every time. Run-in: -13% over 5 days and -19% over 20 days. From 11-13 GOTU is -17% against KWEB -7.8%, FXI -6%, TAL -3%, EDU -6% and DAO -10%. The excess fall came on 11-19 and 11-20 (-5%, then -9.6% against KWEB -2.8% on 11-20), the days Youdao reported Q3 with learning services revenue -5.2%. I found no Gaotu-specific news on those days. Consensus: Q3 revenue RMB1.928B (Chartmill, snippet only, undated), about 3.8% above the top of guidance (RMB1,838-1,858M, +16.4-17.7%), so the habitual guide beat is already in the number. The FY2026 revenue consensus of about RMB7.07B (stockanalysis, targets last dated 2026-03-13) looks stale: it matches management's November 2025 'about 15%' FY comment. Positioning: short interest 1.89% of float (Insider Monkey, 2026-08-28). The cumulative buyback of RMB742M is large against a market cap of about $500M and cash of about RMB4.0B.
view: Gaotu reliably beats the top of its own revenue guide by 2-6% (Q4'25 1,685 vs 1,628-1,648; Q1'26 1,690 vs 1,578-1,598; Q2'26 1,670 vs 1,578-1,598), and the June-quarter leading indicators support another one. Deferred revenue was RMB2.6B (+18.9%) and billings +19.4%. My own deferred-revenue roll puts Q3 revenue at about RMB1.87-1.92B (+18-21%). The street's RMB1.93B already assumes that, so the headline is not where the reaction is decided. The stock has traded on the next-quarter guide, billings and the profit and cash path: Q3'25 sold off on +11% billings and a slower Q4 guide, Q4'25 on a 6-7% Q1 guide, Q1'26 on falling operating income and cash outflow. The one rise came when the guide showed growth holding at 16-18%. Tomorrow turns on the Q4 guide (the base is RMB1,685M, +21% last year) and on Q3 billings against an easy +11% comparison. The inputs lean mildly constructive: one-on-one new-enrolment billings +55% in Q2, college and civil-service courses +40%, offline centres full, the summer-season comparison easy. Against that, management has said profit comes before growth, the guide steps down by habit (Q3 guided at 17% after a 20% quarter), and the FY2026 net-profit ambition (June 2026, the founder) looks out of reach: YTD GAAP net loss is about -RMB101M with Q3 seasonally a loss quarter. The 17% fall over the last nine sessions came mostly with the China tape and Youdao's print, not Gaotu news. That lowers the bar but does not say the release clears it. Net: a slight lean up from the lower bar and the easy billings comparison, not enough to bet on.

recommendation.reason: The habitual revenue beat is already in consensus (RMB1.93B against a guide top of RMB1.858B). The deciding lines are the Q4 guide and Q3 billings, and I can see only their inputs: a strong Q2 deferred-revenue build and an easy billings comparison against a management habit of conservative guides and profit-first rhetoric. The pre-print fall lowers the bar, but it came with the tape, so it is not evidence about the release. Nothing reaches 65%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 guide implying mid-teens or better growth (above about RMB1.94B) with Q3 billings up more than 15% would make it a clear up day. A Q4 guide near or below 10%, or the FY profitability ambition withdrawn, would repeat the -8 to -10% reactions of three of the last four prints.

self_critique: The case for up is stronger than 54 if the 17% pre-print slide was mostly tape: a stock below cash that beats consensus on an easy billings comparison could bounce 8-10%, as it did for +5% in August and +31% in February 2025. The case for down is that this name has fallen on three of the last four prints despite beats, management guides conservatively, and a Q4 guide implying deceleration from a roughly 20% Q3, plus a walked-back profit goal, fits the EDU template exactly. Both cases are live, and that is why I stay near 50.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition was the most useful part: it showed the pre-print fall was mostly tape plus Youdao, not company news. P4 helped confirm with a number that the guide beat sits in consensus. Not seeing the Q4 consensus left the deciding line unanchored, and the playbook offers no route around missing consensus for a thinly covered ADR.
